I’m a patrol officer, so I’m used to juggling calls and reports, but for the past six months or so it feels like my head just doesn’t stay where it’s supposed to be. I’ll be writing up an incident report and miss obvious details, like getting a plate number wrong or leaving whole sections blank. My supervisor has sent things back a few times because of careless mistakes, and it’s not like I don’t know how to do it—I just lose the thread halfway through.

It’s similar at home. My wife will ask me to take care of a couple of simple things—trash, dishes, paying a bill—and I’ll start one, drift off, and somehow none of them get fully done. She thinks I’m ignoring her, but it’s more like I start and then my mind slips away.

Physically, I feel like I can’t settle. Even when I’m off duty, I’m pacing, getting up and down, starting random tasks. My coworkers joke I’m always buzzing around the station. In conversations I end up cutting people off or jumping in before they’re finished, even when I’m trying not to. It’s been wearing on me, and I’m constantly uneasy and tense about messing something up, which just makes it harder to focus.
